# `min-length-decreased`

minLength decreased

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `min-length-decreased` (both directions), `min-length-decreased-in-request`, `min-length-decreased-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`minLength` decreased.

## Why this default

In requests: more strings are valid. In responses: clients may receive shorter (e.g. empty) strings than they expect.

## Example

From test case [`min-length-decreased`](../../test/cases/min-length-decreased/): minLength lowered on a response string.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
-           minLength: 2
+           minLength: 1
```

Findings:

- `min-length-decreased-in-response` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  min-length-decreased: warn
```

## How to fix

Check that clients handle the shorter values.
